overview: Black takes the c-pawn and White regains it at once with 3.e3 and 4.Bxc4 (or 3.Qa4+, 3.Na3), so it is a Queen's Gambit Accepted with the knight already on f3. White gets a slightly freer game and often adds g3/Bg2 or d4; Black aims for ...c5 and ...Nc6 or ...b5 ideas to equalise.

white_ideas.idea: Regain the pawn with Bxc4 (after e3) and build a centre with d4.
Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, or Qa4+/Na3 to win the pawn back by force.

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...c5, counting on a free game.
Hit the bishop on c4 and challenge d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6.

typical_structures.structure: QGA-style open centre with White pawn on d4 and Black pawn on c5/e6.
Isolated queen's pawn or hanging pawns after ...cxd4 exchanges.

character.notes: Normal development and early pawn regain; positions are open but not forcing. Neither side needs to take big risks.

gambit.notes: White regains the c4 pawn at once (3.e3, 3.Qa4+, 3.Na3), so no material is given up for real.

soundness.notes: Fully sound for both sides, equal-ish.

structure.notes: Like the QGA: the c-pawn is gone, the centre opens with d4 and ...c5, play with open lines and IQP-type structures.

approach.notes: A move-order branch of the Réti and the QGA; played by strong players occasionally.

level.notes: Easy to learn, with QGA-style plans to understand; Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Réti Accepted, 3.Qa4+
sublines_that_differ.how: White wins the pawn back with the queen out early; Black blocks with ...Bd7 or ...Nc6 and play is more irregular.

character.reason: QGA-style open play without forcing tactics or a fortress feel.

gambit.reason: White regains the pawn straight away by force, so no gambit.

soundness.reason: Standard, sound development for both sides.

structure.reason: Plays like the QGA with the centre opening up after d4 and ...c5.

approach.reason: A respectable branch of the Réti that strong players use occasionally.

level.reason: Few lines to memorise, but QGA-type structures need understanding.

plans.reason: Typical IQP structures and quick development after the regained pawn.
